note: THERE IS NO PREDICATE CALLED `salary`. Three incompatible conventions are in the sources and pooling them manufactures disagreements out of definitions. The convention is part of the PREDICATE NAME, so pooling is not expressible rather than merely forbidden - the same move as a person having no name.
established: 2026-09-04, from the DocDump scan (report 14) and the §8.4 revision (report 11)

salary_base.definition: base salary only - contracts stripped of bonuses and incentives
sources: NFLPA salary surveys as reported by the Cayman Compass 1986 and the LA Times/AP 1988
salary_base.source_words: "Rankings were determined by players' base salaries, which are contracts stripped of bonuses or incentives."

salary_base_plus_prorated_bonus.definition: base salary plus reporting and roster bonuses plus the signing bonus PRO-RATED over the contract length
sources: Dallas Morning News tables, as carried by UD 1985-01-14 and the Pampa News 1984-10-18
salary_base_plus_prorated_bonus.source_words: "Figures reflect 1984 base salary, reporting and roster bonuses and signing bonus pro-rated over the length of the contract."
salary_base_plus_prorated_bonus.worked_example: Billy Sims: 5-year deal, $1,000,000 bonus, 1984 salary $600,000, prorated bonus $200,000/yr, LISTED at $800,000
salary_base_plus_prorated_bonus.same_as: the NFL Management Council method described in Newman 1987 Appendix C

compensation_component.definition: an itemised line of a real contract, each component its OWN predicate. Never summed by us.
sources: federal court opinions - findings of fact, zero removes
compensation_component.note: This is the only convention that permits reconstructing any of the others. It is also the only one with no attribution chain.

added_2026_09_04.additional_compensation: the source's own words for a component that is neither salary nor a named bonus (Heidel: '$5,000 as additional compensation')
added_2026_09_04.amount_actually_paid: money RECEIVED, as distinct from money contracted. Kapp: $600,000 contracted, $154,000 paid. Filing either as the other is the fifth decoy.
added_2026_09_04.total_earnings_year: a whole year's football income as stipulated for tax purposes - not a contract line (Gardin: $43,326 for 1971)

club_cost_per_player.definition: total club expenditure divided by headcount - INCLUDES benefits, medical, workmen's compensation, payroll taxes, retirement, insurance and pre/post-season pay
sources: the League's figure as quoted by the NFLPA in the 1982 hearing
club_cost_per_player.note: This is what made the §8.4 contest look factual when it was definitional. It is not a salary at all.

qualifying_offer.definition: a CONTRACTUAL THRESHOLD, not a measurement of pay - the minimum a club must offer to retain first-refusal or compensation rights
includes: monetary salary payments for the player's services
qualifying_offer.source: Reynolds v. NFL, 584 F.2d 280 (8th Cir. 1978), quoting the CBA's Article XV
qualifying_offer.source_words: The qualifying offer essentially refers only to monetary salary payments to be made for the player's services or as a bonus for reporting; it does not include non-cash compensation or outside income possibilities.
qualifying_offer.warning: A qualifying offer is a FLOOR a club had to clear, never evidence of what a player was paid. Filing it beside real salaries would read as 16 players earning exactly $30,000.

salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.definition: base salary WITH signing, reporting and roster bonuses included on the NFLPA's method - money attributed to the year it is RECEIVED, not pro-rated across the contract
salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.distinct_from: salary_base_plus_prorated_bonus - the Management Council / Dallas Morning News method, which spreads a signing bonus over the contract length
salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.source: NFLPA survey as published by The Buffalo News, carried in The Register, 9 February 1987
salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.source_words: If signing, reporting and roster bonuses are included as well as base salary...

evidence_it_is_NOT_prorated.argument: Two of 28 team averages are INVERTED - the 'total' is LOWER than the base. Cleveland -$2,404 and Denver -$51,233. Addition cannot produce an inversion, so the two columns are not (base) and (base + bonus) computed over the same money.
evidence_it_is_NOT_prorated.the_source_explains_it: the discrepancy is attributable to bonus payments that have long deferments
evidence_it_is_NOT_prorated.corroborated_by: Newman 1987 Appendix C: 'the Management Council pro-rates signing bonuses by the number of years a player is under contract; the NFLPA defers money to the year it is received'

salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.population: all of a team's players, INCLUDING those who spent the year on injured reserve and did not play
salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.population_words: The figures represent the average pay for all of a team's players, even if the player spent the year on injured reserve and didn't play.
salary_base_plus_bonuses_nflpa.warning: The exact mechanism producing an inversion is NOT determinable from the page. Recorded as the source states it; do not reconstruct the arithmetic.

guaranteed_income_floor.definition: A FLOOR on the player's earnings from OUTSIDE EMPLOYMENT, which the club tops up if he falls short. It is not pay for football and it is not a payment at all until a shortfall exists.
guaranteed_income_floor._it_is_the_INVERSE_of_a_salary: a salary is paid for playing. This is paid BECAUSE HE EARNED TOO LITTLE ELSEWHERE. The club's liability falls as the player's outside income rises, so filing a scheduled amount as compensation would record as received a sum the club may never have owed.
includes: the scheduled floor for a named calendar year
excludes: playing salary, which is in the Player Contract
whatever the Ancillary Rights Agreement covers
any amount actually paid, which the document does not state

mechanism.offset: compensation from Outside Employment - defined in the instrument as personal services for compensation other than under the Player Contract or the Ancillary Rights Agreement - is set against the floor
mechanism.clawback: if the club pays under the agreement and the player later exceeds a listed year's figure, he repays the excess by 10 January following
mechanism._consequence: the schedule is a CEILING on the club's exposure and a FLOOR on the player's income. It is neither a salary nor a bonus, and it resolves to an amount only once outside earnings are known - which no source we hold states.

hard_rules: A guaranteed_income_floor_year figure is NOT salary_base and must never be pooled with one, averaged with one, or rendered as what a man was paid.
It is a SCHEDULED FLOOR, not a payment. Absent a statement of outside earnings, the amount actually transferred is unknown - an `unknown` base, not a zero and not the scheduled figure.
A floor scheduled for a year the player did not play, or did not live to see, is still a fact about the instrument. It is not a fact about his career.

worked_example._status: RELAYED, NOT INGESTED - the document is held by Ryan and has not reached this project. Recorded to fix the SHAPE, not the figures.
worked_example.instrument: Cleveland Browns, signed Ernest Davis, Art Modell, Paul Brown, corporate seal dated 1961
worked_example._why_it_matters: nothing else in the collection has this shape. Five other figures relayed alongside it are ordinary salaries; this one is a different instrument and would have been silently mis-filed as salary_base.

guaranteed_income_floor.added_2026_09_05: the first convention added from an instrument rather than from a newspaper's or a court's description of one

unpaid_wages_settlement.definition: A sum a club FAILED to pay, scheduled for later repayment. It is the record of money NOT received, not of money received.
unpaid_wages_settlement._the_inversion: filing it as salary records the exact opposite of what happened. Sam Silas's $15,749.95 is what the Portland Storm did not pay him.
unpaid_wages_settlement.instrument: ADDENDUM TO 1974 PLAYER'S CONTRACT - between the player, 'A Club in the 1975 World Football League', and the WFL itself as a non-profit corporation

quotes.novation: such 1974 WFL Club is not a necessary party since it failed to fulfil its basic contractual obligation to pay player for services rendered. Player is no longer bound to such 1974 Club... hereby extinguish the 1974 Standard WFL Player's Contract with this unconditional addendum.
quotes.payment: Club will pay to Player a total sum of $15,749.95 in the following installments: (which is undisputedly owed to Player)

mechanism.first: not more than 15% on completion of the WFL Reorganization, no later than 30 April 1975
mechanism.balance: semi-annual installments on 1 March and 1 September from September 1975, at SIX PER CENT simple annual interest on unpaid principal
mechanism.funded_from: the WFL Contingency Fund - the club deposits 1% of net ticket receipts, 1% of net income from WFL properties, 1/10% of net revenues per $20,000 assigned, and 5% of net national television revenues from 1976
mechanism._consequence: the player's recovery depends on the LEAGUE's revenues, not his club's promise. Whether he was ever paid is unknown and not in the document.

hard_rules: An unpaid_wages_owed figure is NOT salary and must never be pooled with one. It is a debt, and the amount actually recovered is UNKNOWN.
The 1974 WFL contract it extinguishes is a DIFFERENT instrument. This addendum does not state what he was contracted to earn, only what he was owed and unpaid.
unpaid_wages_settlement.added_2026_09_05: read from the Sam Silas addendum; Wallace Williams carries the identical header, so the Portland Storm batch is settlements, not contracts

version_A_Silas.obligor: 'Club will pay to Player a total sum of $15,749.95'
version_A_Silas.schedule: semi-annual installments on March 1 and September 1 from September 1975, 6% simple annual interest

version_B_Billingsley.obligor: 'Club AND WORLD FOOTBALL LEAGUE will pay to Player a total sum of $31,500.00'
version_B_Billingsley.schedule: principal balance in TEN (10) annual installments, semi-annually on March 1st and September 1st

TWO_VERSIONS_OF_THE_ADDENDUM._why_it_matters: in one version the league is a CO-OBLIGOR and in the other it is not. That changes who owed the money, which is the whole substance of the instrument. A transcription that captured only the figure would lose it.
TWO_VERSIONS_OF_THE_ADDENDUM._also_seen: bleed-through from the reverse of the Billingsley sheet reads 'provide for a minimum of $1,000.00 per regularly scheduled season game for which Player is on active status' - a per-game minimum in the 1975 contract the addendum promises. Not yet read directly; recorded as a lead, not a figure.

_counterparts_are_not_separate_instrumen.case: Ron Billingsley appears in two Kayfabe lots (398120727238 and 257594925421). Both are ADDENDUM TO 1974 PLAYER'S CONTRACT, both $31,500.00, identical wording.
_counterparts_are_not_separate_instrumen.conclusion: two counterparts of ONE instrument, not two documents. Counting them as two would double a debt that was owed once.
_counterparts_are_not_separate_instrumen.rule: a second listing of the same instrument is a counterpart until its FIGURE or its TERMS differ. Check before treating it as new.

postseason_pool_share.definition: A player's share of a league-administered postseason player pool, paid BY THE LEAGUE, not by the club.
postseason_pool_share.instrument: NFL memorandum over Pete Rozelle's name, '1966 NFL Championship Game'
postseason_pool_share.quote: Enclosed is a check from the National Football League in the amount of $9813.63 which constitutes the payment of your share of the player pool of the championship game played on 1 January 1967 at Dallas, Texas.
postseason_pool_share.gross: 'no deductions have been taken from your share for Federal income tax' - the figure is GROSS, which most salary figures in this collection are not stated to be either way
hard_rules: A postseason pool share is paid by the LEAGUE and must not be attributed to the club, nor pooled with club salary.
It is per-GAME and per-postseason, not per-season, and belongs to the game it names.
postseason_pool_share._why_it_is_new: nothing in the archive held postseason compensation of any kind. The 182 salary figures are all club-paid regular-season pay.

hard_rules: A bare `salary` predicate is REFUSED at ingest. The convention is in the name.
Resolution never compares across conventions. Two figures under different conventions are not a contest; they are two measurements of two quantities.
A source declaration must name the convention it uses, per predicate, or its salary claims are ineligible.
An export that scales to a league average must state which convention that average was drawn on, in its manifest.

A guaranteed income floor is not compensation. It is an obligation contingent on the player's OTHER earnings, and it enters as guaranteed_income_floor_year on a contract subject, never as salary_base.

non_salary_figures_that_look_like_salari.what: the COURT's estimate of free-market value over three years
contracted total, of which only $154,000 was paid
an inter-CLUB release fee paid by Minnesota to Kapp's Canadian club
non_salary_figures_that_look_like_salari.note: a transfer price - the sixth decoy, and the only one that is a real payment to a real party

system_rules._note: Claims about how the SYSTEM worked, not about what a person was paid. They take a league-season or league-era subject and can never take a person. Enforced at ingest, so averaging them with player money is not expressible - the same move as the salary conventions themselves.
hard_rules: A system_rule predicate REQUIRES a league-scoped subject and REFUSES a person.
A money predicate about a person REFUSES a league-scoped subject.
So a system rule can never enter a player-salary average: the subject types do not meet.

sources_searched_and_empty.source: Robertson v. NBA (cited in the Reynolds and Newman lines)
sources_searched_and_empty.result: one dollar figure, a statutory penalty
sources_searched_and_empty.note: recorded as an ABSENCE so the next session does not repeat the search - design 3.4

sources_searched_and_empty.source: The Business of Football 2001 (Carmel, CA: Paul Kagan Associates, Inc., 2001)
sources_searched_and_empty.searched_for: a 1968-1982 salary series; cited by CRS RL34439 for labour and economic history
sources_searched_and_empty.result: NOT HELD ANYWHERE SEARCHABLE. Zero archive.org hits for the title; the only 'Paul Kagan Associates' hit in the entire archive is a 1985 Newsweek broadcast.
sources_searched_and_empty.deflating_evidence: the CRS cites it exactly FIVE times, pages 392-396 - five consecutive pages, all supporting the labour CHRONOLOGY. An author writing on NFL player compensation who had a salary series in hand would have cited it for one. The shape was promising; the citation pattern says chronology, not series.

sources_searched_and_empty.source: archive.org FULL-TEXT search (not catalogue) for the Management Council table
sources_searched_and_empty.searched_for: "highest salary paid"+"lowest salary paid"+football; "NFL Management Council"+salary; "average salary by position"+football
sources_searched_and_empty.result: NOT FOUND. Full-text search reaches inside access-restricted items, so this was the last untried method. Staudohar WAS found this way, but its 'average salary by position' table is BASEBALL (Table 2.2, p.30) and its four Management Council hits are CBA text and footnotes.
sources_searched_and_empty.note: a finding about the document, not about searching

owed_league_original.what: a document in which the NFL states its own numbers, first-hand
owed_league_original.location: National Archives, federal case file, Mackey v. NFL, docket 4-72-Civil 277
owed_league_original.holds: ~400 trial exhibits including financial exhibits produced by the clubs
owed_league_original.why_it_is_different: League-original. Every source held reaches the League's figures through the NFLPA, a newspaper, an agent or a court's summary of them.
owed_league_original.if_never_obtained: a legitimate resting state - §8.4 stays at one party and one hearsay, which the design already records

_decoy_kinds.not_compensation: never money paid to a player for playing. BLOCK on the write - these must not reach a money predicate at all.
_decoy_kinds.requires_pairing: real compensation data that is easily misread as something else. ADMIT under its own predicate, but REQUIRE the companion figure in the same case so the pair travels together.
_decoy_kinds._why: The first list conflated 'false' with 'easily misread'. Kapp's $600,000 is a genuine contracted total and blocking it discards a real figure; the danger is reading it as money received, which is prevented by admitting $154,000 alongside it under amount_actually_paid.

cohort_aggregates._note: A positional or service-year average describes a COHORT, not a person and not a league rule. Person-money predicates refuse a cohort subject and vice versa, so an aggregate can never be averaged with individual pay.

predicates.cohort_salary_average: mean pay across the cohort, on a STATED convention
predicates.cohort_size: n - how many players the aggregate is over

cohort_aggregates.why_it_matters: This is the SHAPE of the owed Management Council table (position x service year, high/low/average/median per cell). Building the scope now means that document drops straight in if it is ever obtained.

_decoy_scoping: A decoy is a figure IN A DOCUMENT, never a number in the abstract. Keyed on value alone the list blocked Ray Guy's genuine $150,000 punter salary in the 1984 UD table, because a 1968 agent's deposition estimate in Smith happened to be the same round number. Round numbers are attractors - the same precedent that rejected Manning's $600,000 as corroboration. Each decoy now carries the source it belongs to and fires only there.

_documentation_only.established: the date a ruling was made
_documentation_only.sources_searched_and_empty: a negative result - what was searched and held nothing
_documentation_only.owed_league_original: a record of a document not obtained, and the decision about it
_documentation_only._rule: keys addressed to a reader and to no code path. Everything NOT listed here must be read by something in src/ - see src/gate_declarations_are_read.py. This list living in the declaration rather than in the gate means widening it shows up in a diff.
_documentation_only.contract_images: a source record and its rights constraint; the enforceable parts are the acquisition classes already in 3.7

transfer_payments._note: A payment from one CLUB to another for a player's release or rights. It is not a salary - the player is not the payee - and it is not a system rule, because it is one transaction on one date rather than a statement of how the regime worked.
transfer_payments._ruling: 2026-09-04, Ryan. inter_club_transfer_fee was declared under system_rules.predicates, which requires a league-scoped subject. Filing this figure on the league would state a RULE where there is an INSTANCE - the same error as pooling conventions, one level up.
transfer_payments.why_this_shape: it preserves everything the source states: which man, which two clubs, which date. A league subject loses all three. It extends the ('contract', person, club) shape that resolved the two-Kapp-contracts false contest, rather than inventing a new idea.
hard_rules: A transfer predicate REQUIRES a transfer-scoped subject and REFUSES a league, person or cohort subject.
A person-scoped money predicate REFUSES a transfer subject: the payee is a club, not the player.
A transfer subject names BOTH clubs. A fee with one club is not a transfer; it is an unresolved claim.

contract_images._what: Auction-listing scans of player contracts, fetched so that readings are TRANSCRIPTIONS of held documents rather than relays.

RIGHTS.constraint: an auction image belongs to the auction house. Held for private reference and citation only. The dataset cites the FIGURE and the LOT; it never republishes the scan. pgm3-sources is outside the repo and stays there.
RIGHTS.alongside: the eBay API note already in the spec

hosts.i.ebayimg.com: s-l1600 is the ceiling; larger names return identical bytes, so the seller's upload sets the limit
hosts.dyn1.heritagestatic.com: it=product IS the full version - 1650x3000 and 1767x3000 measured. Every other it= value returns HTTP 400, so one test settled it rather than thirty low-resolution fetches.

LEGIBILITY_IS_NOT_GUARANTEED_BY_POSSESSI.finding: holding the image does not mean the figure is readable. Groza 1951 is certain at 1767x3000; Leo Sugar 1961 reads '13,?00.00' at 578x949 and the middle digit cannot be resolved at any available size.
LEGIBILITY_IS_NOT_GUARANTEED_BY_POSSESSI.rule: a transcription carries the legibility of the image it was read from. An uncertain digit must travel as uncertain - the same rule as '(date approximate)', and the fourth instance of a value presented at a confidence its derivation does not support.

STRUCTURAL_FINDING.what: the NFL Standard Players Contract states its own PAYMENT SCHEDULE: '75% of said salary in weekly installments commencing with the first and ending with the last regularly scheduled League game ... and the balance of 25% of said sum at the end of said last regularly scheduled League game.'
STRUCTURAL_FINDING.why_it_matters: the archive holds 182 salary figures and NO payment structure. This is on the standard form, so it plausibly applies to every contract of the era - which makes it a LEAGUE-scoped system fact, not a per-player one.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING.not_yet_a_claim: it wants its own predicate and a check of how far the clause persists across eras before anything is written.

PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_PERSISTENCE._CORRECTED: 2026-09-05, hours after report 48. I wrote that the 75/25 clause spans 'at least 1951-1961'. It is on the NFL UNIFORM PLAYER'S CONTRACT in 1923 - twenty-eight years earlier - and it is NEGOTIABLE, which I had no evidence of. Both halves of my statement were wrong: the start date and the character.

1923.form: The National Football League UNIFORM PLAYER'S CONTRACT
1923.printed_default: Seventy-five per cent (75%) after each game and the remaining twenty-five per cent (25%) at the close of the season or upon release
1923.AS_EXECUTED: struck through and amended BY HAND to Ninety per cent (90%) after each game and ten per cent (10%) at the close
1923.player: Walter J. Pearce, Chicago Bears, $85.00 PER GAME, signed 24 August 1923 by Geo. S. Halas
1923._what_it_proves: the schedule is a PRINTED DEFAULT that individual contracts could override, not a fixed league rule. A transcription reading the printed text would record 75/25 for a man who negotiated 90/10.

PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_PERSISTENCE.1938: the Union City / American Professional Football Association form carries paragraph 1 in NEARLY IDENTICAL WORDING to the 1923 NFL form - 'As to games scheduled but not played the player shall receive no compensation from the Club, other than actual expenses'. The minor league used a form derived from the NFL's. Its own schedule was handwritten: paid after each game.
PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_PERSISTENCE.1951_1954_1961: 75% weekly / 25% at the last regularly scheduled game, printed, and unamended in Groza, Atkins and Sugar
PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_PERSISTENCE.1969: CHANGED - percentages blank on the form, semi-monthly installments, compensation subject to Paragraph 7 and changeable under Paragraph 10
PAYMENT_SCHEDULE_PERSISTENCE._conclusion: a printed default present from at least 1923, per-GAME in the 1920s and per-WEEK by 1951, negotiable at least in 1923, and replaced by a blank-percentage semi-monthly form by 1969. It is a form-level fact, not a league rule, and what any given player was actually paid on requires reading HIS contract rather than the era's.

1966_67_Gregg._SECOND_CORRECTION: my table listed 1951/1954/1961 as '75/25 weekly' and 1969 as 'blank percentages, semi-monthly', treating it as ONE change. It is TWO.
1966_67_Gregg.as_read: 75% of said salary in equal SEMI-MONTHLY installments commencing with the first regularly scheduled League game played by the Club during each season and continuing each semi-monthly period thereafter; The balance of 25% ... on the date of the last regularly scheduled League game.
1966_67_Gregg.so: the percentages are still a printed 75/25 in 1966, but the INTERVAL has already changed from weekly to semi-monthly. Two independent changes: weekly -> semi-monthly between 1961 and 1966, and fixed 75/25 -> blank percentages between 1966 and 1969.
1966_67_Gregg._lesson: I read two variables as one because they changed in the same clause. A schedule has an interval AND a split, and they moved separately.

LEAGUE_NAME_COLLISION.trap: the 1938 Franco contract says 'The American Professional Football Association'. That is a 1930s MINOR league. StatsCrew's APFA code means the 1920-21 league that became the NFL.
LEAGUE_NAME_COLLISION.danger: same shape as AFL3 resolving to the Arena Football League: a name that reads as a league we already hold, describing a different one.
LEAGUE_NAME_COLLISION.rule: a league named in a contract is the CONTRACT'S league, resolved against the era, never assumed to be the code we happen to use for that string.

PORTLAND_STORM_BATCH_IS_NOT_CONTRACTS.expected: thirteen 1974 Portland Storm player contracts from one club in one season
PORTLAND_STORM_BATCH_IS_NOT_CONTRACTS.actual: thirteen WFL DEBT SETTLEMENTS. Every one read so far is an 'ADDENDUM TO 1974 PLAYER'S CONTRACT' extinguishing the original and scheduling repayment of wages the club failed to pay.
PORTLAND_STORM_BATCH_IS_NOT_CONTRACTS.verified: Sam Silas (read in full) and Wallace Williams (header identical)
PORTLAND_STORM_BATCH_IS_NOT_CONTRACTS.why_it_matters: the figures would have entered as 1974 WFL salaries. They are the opposite: sums the club did not pay. The batch is more historically interesting than a salary set - it is the WFL's collapse, documented player by player - but it answers a different question.

instances: 1923 Pearce - 75/25 struck through, amended to 90/10 by hand
1938 Franco - paragraph 4's release proviso struck through entirely
A_DELETION_IS_DATA.rule: a struck-through clause is a NEGOTIATED TERM and must be read as such. Reading only the printed text records the opposite of what the parties agreed, and no OCR pass catches a strike-through.
A_DELETION_IS_DATA._consequence: any future contract ingest must capture the AS-EXECUTED text, not the form's text. This is not a transcription convenience - it is the difference between what was printed and what was agreed.

OPTION_YEAR_RATE_CONFIRMED_IN_AN_INSTRUM.quote: the Club may fix the rate of compensation to be paid by the Club to the Player during said period of renewal, which compensation shall not be less than ninety percent (90%) of the amount paid by the Club to the Player during the preceding season
OPTION_YEAR_RATE_CONFIRMED_IN_AN_INSTRUM.source: NFL Standard Players Contract, Green Bay Packers / Forrest Gregg, 1966 and 1967, paragraph 10
OPTION_YEAR_RATE_CONFIRMED_IN_AN_INSTRUM.why_it_matters: option_year_rate = 0.90 is already a declared SYSTEM predicate in this project, taken from secondary description. This is the rule stated in the INSTRUMENT ITSELF - a primary source for a system fact we had only at one remove.
OPTION_YEAR_RATE_CONFIRMED_IN_AN_INSTRUM.also_in_paragraph_10: 'the phrase rate of compensation as above used shall not be understood to include bonus payments or payments of any nature whatsoever other than the precise sum set forth in Paragraph 3' - the 90% applies to BASE ONLY, which is exactly the convention distinction salary_base exists to preserve.
